name: Ulysses
best_known_for: First spacecraft to observe the Sun's poles from above + below the ecliptic — used a Jupiter gravity assist in 1992 to flip into a polar heliocentric orbit, then surveyed the heliosphere for 18 years
credit: Joint ESA + NASA solar / heliospheric mission, built by Dornier with US scientific contribution. Launched 1990-10-06 from STS-41 Discovery + IUS + PAM-S on a high-energy trajectory direct to Jupiter — the only way to fling a spacecraft out of the ecliptic plane without prohibitive delta-v. Jupiter flyby 1992-02-08 deflected the spacecraft into an 80°-inclination heliocentric orbit (1.3 × 5.4 AU, 6.2-year period) — the first and still only spacecraft ever to fly over the Sun's poles. Three pairs of polar passes (approximately 2.5 solar orbits) gave us the heliospheric current sheet 3D structure, the solar wind's faster polar streams + slower equatorial belt, in-situ cosmic-ray latitudinal gradients, and the only multi-decade record of polar coronal hole behaviour over a complete solar cycle. Mission ended 2009-06-30 when the X-band transmitter heater failed.
